en: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us (H); and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from as-Suddi, from Yahya ibn Abbad, from Anas: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about wine being turned into vinegar, and he said: "No."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Bakr—meaning al-Hanafi—narrated to us: Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us: my father narrated to me that he heard Anas ibn Malik saying: Allah indeed revealed the verse in which Allah prohibited wine, while in Medina there was no beverage being drunk except that made from dates.

And Abu at-Tahir, Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Abdallah ibn Wahb informed us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Qatadah ibn Di'amah narrated to him that he heard Anas ibn Malik saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that dried dates and partially ripened dates (zahw) be mixed together and then drunk; and that was the common wine of theirs on the day wine was prohibited.

And Abu at-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Ishaq ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, that he said: I was serving Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Abu Talhah, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b a drink made from fadhikh (unripe date wine) and dried dates, when a person came to them and said: "Indeed, wine has been prohibited." Abu Talhah said: "O Anas, get up and break this jar." So I went to a stone mortar of ours and struck it with the bottom of it until it broke.

And Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—they said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham informed us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I was indeed serving Abu Talhah, Abu Dujanah, and Suhayl ibn Bayda' from a large water skin containing a mixture of unripe dates and dried dates... a narration similar to the hadith of Sa'id.

And Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us; he said: And Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I was serving Abu Talhah, Abu Dujanah, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal among a group of the Ansar, when someone entered upon us and said: "News has arrived: the prohibition of wine has been revealed." So on that day we spilled it, and it was a mixture of unripe dates and dried dates. Qatadah said: And Anas ibn Malik said: "Wine was indeed prohibited, and most of their wine on that day was a mixture of unripe dates and dried dates."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: Anas said: "I was standing serving the people of the clan..." a narration similar to the hadith of Ibn Ulayyah, except that he said: Abu Bakr ibn Anas said: "It was their wine on that day," while Anas was present and Anas did not deny that. And Ibn Abd al-A'la said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: One of those who was with me narrated to me that he heard Anas saying: "It was their wine on that day."

And Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us; he said: And Sulayman at-Taymi informed us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: I was standing serving the people of the clan—my paternal uncles—serving them from their fadhikh, while I was the youngest of them in age. A man came and said: "Indeed, wine has been prohibited." So they said: "Spill it, O Anas." So I spilled it. He said: I said to Anas: "What was it?" He said: "Unripe dates and fresh ripe dates." He said: Then Abu Bakr ibn Anas said: "It was their wine on that day." Sulayman said: And a man narrated to me from Anas ibn Malik that he said that as well.

And Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb informed us, who said: They asked Anas ibn Malik about al-fadhikh, and he said: We had no wine other than this fadhikh of yours that you call al-fadhikh. I was standing serving it to Abu Talhah, Abu Ayyub, and men from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in our house, when a man came and said: "Has the news reached you?" We said: "No." He said: "Wine has been prohibited." So he said: "O Anas, pour out these jars." He said: And they never returned to it nor inquired about it after the news from that man.

Abu ar-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Ataki narrated to me: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us: Thabit informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I was serving the people drink on the day wine was prohibited in the house of Abu Talhah, and their drink was nothing other than fadhikh: unripe dates and dried dates. Suddenly a caller was calling out, so he said: "Go out and see." So I went out, and behold, a caller was calling out: "Lo, wine has been prohibited!" He said: So it flowed through the alleyways of Medina. Then Abu Talhah said to me: "Go out and spill it." So I spilled it. Then they said—or some of them said—: "So-and-so was killed, so-and-so was killed while it was in their bellies"—he said: so I do not know if that was from the hadith of Anas—whereupon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they consumed, provided they fear Allah, believe, and do righteous deeds} [Surah Al-Ma'idah, 5:93].

And Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Quhzadh narrated it to me: Abdallah ibn Uthman narrated to me, from Abdallah ibn al-Mubarak, from Yunus, from az-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Ufayr Abu Uthman al-Misri informed us: Abdallah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: Ali ibn Husayn ibn Ali informed me that Husayn ibn Ali informed him that Ali said: I had an old she-camel from my share of the spoils on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had given me another old she-camel from the fifth that day. When I intended to consummate my marriage with Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), I made an arrangement with a goldsmith from Banu Qaynuqa' to travel with me so that we could bring idhkhir grass, which I intended to sell to the goldsmiths to help finance my wedding feast. While I was gathering equipment for my two she-camels of pack-saddles, sacks, and ropes, and my two she-camels were kneeling beside the room of a man of the Ansar, and having gathered what I had gathered, suddenly I found that both of my she-camels had their humps cut off, their flanks slashed open, and their livers taken out. I could not control my tears when I saw that sight of them. I said: "Who did this?" They said: "Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib did it, and he is in this house in a drinking party of the Ansar; a singing-girl was singing to him and his companions, saying in her song: 'O Hamzah, come upon the plump she-camels!' So Hamzah leapt with the sword, chopped off their humps, slashed open their flanks, and took from their livers." Ali said: So I set off until I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), while Zayd ibn Harithah was with him. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) recognized in my face what I had encountered. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "What is the matter with you?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have never seen the like of today! Hamzah attacked my two she-camels, chopped off their humps, slashed open their flanks, and here he is in a house with a drinking party." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for his cloak, put it on, and set off walking, and Zayd ibn Harithah and I followed him until he came to the door where Hamzah was. He asked permission to enter, and they granted him permission, and behold, they were a drinking party. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) began reproaching Hamzah for what he had done, but behold, Hamzah's eyes were bloodshot. Hamzah looked at the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), then raised his gaze to his knees, then raised his gaze to his navel, then raised his gaze to his face, and Hamzah said: "Are you anything other than slaves to my father?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) realized that he was drunk, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stepped back on his heels, retreated backwards, and walked out, and we walked out with him.
And Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd ar-Razzaq informed me: Ibn Jurayj informed me, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

Yahya ibn Yahya at-Tamimi narrated to us: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ibn Jurayj: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from Ali ibn Husayn ibn Ali, from his father, Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: I obtained an old she-camel along with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in the booty on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gave me another old she-camel. One day, I made them kneel at the door of a man of the Ansar while intending to carry idhkhir grass on them to sell it, having with me a goldsmith from Banu Qaynuqa', in order to help me with the feast for Fatimah. Meanwhile, Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib was drinking in that house, accompanied by a singing-girl who sang to him, saying: "O Hamzah, come upon the plump she-camels!" So Hamzah leapt toward them with the sword, chopped off their humps, slashed open their flanks, and took from their livers. I said to Ibn Shihab: "And from the hump?" He said: "He chopped off their humps and took them away." Ibn Shihab said: Ali said: "I looked at a sight that horrified me, so I came to the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), while Zayd ibn Harithah was with him, and informed him of the news. He came out with Zayd, and I went along with him. He entered upon Hamzah and showed anger towards him, but Hamzah raised his eyes and said: 'Are you anything other than slaves to my fathers?' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stepped back, retreating backwards until he left them."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrating from Abu at-Tufayl, who said: Ali was asked: "Did the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) single you out for anything?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not single us out for anything that he did not make common to all the people, except for what is in this sheath of my sword." He said: So he brought out a document in which was written: "May Allah curse whoever slaughters to other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever steals the boundary markers of the land; may Allah curse whoever curses his parent; and may Allah curse whoever harbors an innovator."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, Sulayman ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Hayyan, from Abu at-Tufayl, who said: We said to Ali ibn Abi Talib: "Inform us of something that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) confided to you." He said: "He did not confide anything to me that he concealed from the people, but I heard him saying: 'May Allah curse whoever slaughters to other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever harbors an innovator; may Allah curse whoever curses his parents; and may Allah curse whoever changes the boundary markers.'"

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us—both from Marwan; Zuhayr said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us: Mansur ibn Hayyan narrated to us: Abu at-Tufayl Amir ibn Wathilah narrated to us, who said: I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib when a man came to him and said: "What did the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) use to confide to you in secret?" He said: He became angry and said: "The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) never confided anything to me that he concealed from the people, except that he related to me four statements." He said: The man said: "What are they, O Commander of the Believers?" He said: He said: "May Allah curse whoever curses his parent; may Allah curse whoever slaughters to other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever harbors an innovator; and may Allah curse whoever alters the boundary markers of the land."

And Harmalah ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Akhi Ibn Wahb narrated to me—both saying: Abdallah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Haywah informed me: Khalid ibn Yazid informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Umar ibn Muslim al-Junda'i, that Ibn al-Musayyab informed him that Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), informed him... and he mentioned from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with the meaning of their hadith.

Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me: Amr ibn Muslim ibn Ammar al-Laythi narrated to us, who said: We were in the public bath shortly before al-Adha, and some people used depilatory paste in it. Some of the people of the bath said: "Indeed, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab dislikes this or forbids it." So I met Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and mentioned that to him. He said: "O nephew, this is a hadith that has been forgotten and neglected. Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), narrated to me; she said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said..." with the meaning of the hadith of Mu'adh from Muhammad ibn Amr.

And Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-Anbari narrated to me: my father narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi narrated to us, from Umar ibn Muslim ibn Ammar ibn Ukaymah al-Laythi, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab saying: I heard Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever has a sacrificial animal to slaughter, when the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah is sighted, let him not take anything from his hair or his nails until he has offered the sacrifice."

And Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hakam al-Hashimi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Umar—or Amr—ibn Muslim, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

And Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: Yahya ibn Kathir al-Anbari Abu Ghassan narrated to me: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Umar ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umm Salamah: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When you see the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah and one of you intends to offer a sacrifice, let him refrain from cutting his hair and his nails."

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Sufyan informed us: Abd ar-Rahman ibn Humayd ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umm Salamah, elevating it to the Prophet: he said: "When the ten days enter and someone has a sacrificial animal he intends to sacrifice, let him not take any hair nor clip any nail."

Ibn Abi Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Humayd ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, who heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrating from Umm Salamah: that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When the ten days enter and one of you intends to offer a sacrifice, let him not touch anything of his hair or skin." It was said to Sufyan: "Some of them do not elevate it to the Prophet." He said: "But I elevate it."

And Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: ad-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I had forbidden you..." and he mentioned the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Abu Sinan.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—both saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us; Abu Bakr said: from Abu Sinan, and Ibn al-Muthanna said: from Dirar ibn Murrah, from Muharib, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father (H); and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us: Dirar ibn Murrah Abu Sinan narrated to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Abdallah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them; and I had forbidden you from the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days, so keep whatever seems good to you; and I had forbidden you from nabidh except in a water skin, so drink from all kinds of vessels, but do not drink anything that intoxicates."

Yahya ibn Yahya at-Tamimi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr an-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—Yahya said "informed us" and the others said "narrated to us"—: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) (H); and Muhammad ibn Rafi' and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—Abd said "informed us" and Ibn Rafi' said "narrated to us"—: Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no Fara' and no 'Atirah." Ibn Rafi' added in his narration: "And al-Fara' was the first offspring born to their livestock which they used to slaughter."

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abu Mushir informed us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us: az-Zubaydi narrated to me, from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Prepare this meat." He said: So I prepared it, and he continued eating from it until he reached Medina. And Abdallah ibn Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated it to me: Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he did not say "during the Farewell Pilgrimage."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Rafi' narrated to us—both saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us (H); and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, both from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, with this chain of narration.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ma'n ibn Isa narrated to us: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Abu az-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) slaughtered his sacrificial animal, then said: "O Thawban, prepare the meat of this one." So I continued feeding him from it until he arrived in Medina.
